purpose: Decide whether the stable-masked 3DEP 2018 key (artifacts/reference/3dep-jax068-east/stable) agrees with DFC2019 in shape. Model grading removes one constant vertical offset (dsmr registration), so a constant datum offset between keys does not change grades; shape differences would.
procedure: Same pixels as the failed absolute qualification: labelled in both DFC2019 and the stable 3DEP key, inside the DFC2019 JAX_068 grid.
Offset = median(3DEP - DFC2019) over all compared pixels. Subtract it once from every 3DEP pixel. No horizontal shift, no scaling, no per-class or per-area offsets.
Report the offset, then the residual statistics below.

justification.all_labelled_mae: Same 0.5 m limit as the absolute qualification, now after removing the single constant offset that grading also removes.
justification.ground_mae: Open ground is the most stable surface between 2015 and 2018 and has no edge or vegetation effects; 0.3 m is the absolute qualification's median tolerance.
justification.quadrant_offset_spread: The median offset in each of the four quadrants of the compared area must lie within 0.2 m of the overall offset, so the difference is a uniform datum step rather than a tilt or local distortion.
justification.min_pixels: The failed qualification compared 164,737 pixels; require at least 50,000 so the check is not decided by a small area.

outcome_if_passed: The stable 3DEP key qualifies for shape and may grade the neighbour experiment with registered metrics only; absolute (unregistered) 3DEP heights remain unqualified unless the datum is documented.
outcome_if_failed: 3DEP does not qualify; the neighbour experiment needs another reference.
result: training/3dep-shape-check.json (2026-10-30): failed ground_mae 0.333 > 0.3 m; all-labelled 0.470 m, quadrant spread 0.014 m and min pixels passed; offset -1.577 m. DFC2019 documents WGS84 Z (pubgeo/dfc2019 data/README.md), so the conversion was not changed.
